newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks seen correcting before testing new highs.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen correcting before testing new highs.

text.p: The Hong Kong bourse, which has soared by over 4,000 points or 35 percent since April, is expected to give back at least 1,000 points of that gain in the next few months, before scaling new peaks by the end of the year, Guinness Flight Hambro Asia Ltd said on Monday.

"From here, I would feel much more comfortable if Hong Kong has a correction of about five to 10 percent from the current level, i.e. to about 15,000," Nerissa Lee, director at the fund management firm, told a news conference.
"I think if it does have a correction, then we can look forward to a record high about the year end. I think it can challenge 18,000," she said.
That year-end target will not be achieved without the expected downward adjustment in the short term, she said.
"We have seen an eight percent rise in two weeks," Lee noted. The index, which closed at a record high of 16,379.22 on Friday, finished Monday's session at 16,259.59.
Guinness managing director Royce Brennan said the market is heading for an upward re-rating to come more in line with other Asian markets as political confidence returns.
Investors have perceived little change or risks since Britain returned the former colony to China on July 1, he said.
"In my opinion there is no reason why Hong Kong should trade at a discount -- currently 13 times 1997 price earnings -- to its regional counterparts," he said.

"We will remain overweight in Hong Kong in the third quarter as this re-rating, coupled with earnings growth as strong as 15 percent for the market as a whole, plus economic recovery in China, continues to support the market," he said.
Lee said the market's valuation was attractive and Hong Kong's growing economy would also help the stocks.
"Long term, we are still very positive, very confident in the stock market here," she said. "We have accelerating economic growth in a very favourable interest rate environment."
"The market at the moment is not anticipating any interest rate hikes in the U.S in the short term. So that is positive on the market," she said.
Hong Kong interest rate movements often follow those in the U.S. as the local currency is pegged to the U.S. dollar.
"The strategy is to be slightly underweight in the property sector and red chip but remain positive on stocks specifics," Lee said.

The property sector was subject to uncertainties over the local government's housing policy, while red chips -- or Hong Kong-listed firms with Chinese financial banking -- also looked vulnerable to Beijing's policy, she said.
She expected China to further redirect credit into priority sectors such as petrochemical and infrastructure industries.
The firm urged investors to be selective in investment.
"Over the next six months we expect the market to be dominated by stock-picking, with share prices being drive by corporate activity rather than fundamentals," Brennan said.
